Euro Area Recession Risk Indicator

Replicating Giannone & Furno (Nowcasting Recession Risk)

Author

Automated Report

Welcome to the Euro Area Recession Risk Tracker. This page presents nowcasts of recession probabilities for the Euro Area (EA) and its four largest member states: Germany (DE), France (FR), Italy (IT), and Spain (ES).

Our methodology builds on the Bayesian logit nowcasting framework proposed by Furno and Giannone (2024). By utilizing a Hierarchical Bayesian model, we allow the model to share information across different regions. This hierarchical structure (“shrinkage”) is particularly valuable for improving the reliability of country-specific nowcasts during periods of high economic uncertainty. See Methodology for the full model specification.

Code 
# The dashboard renders from the committed artifacts produced by
# new_code/update_dashboard_data.R (run on a host with RJSDMX/brms, e.g.
# production: DASHBOARD_PREDICTOR=esi Rscript --vanilla new_code/update_dashboard_data.R).
# It never downloads data or fits models here.

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(zoo)
library(scales)

data_dir <- file.path("..", "dashboard", "data")
if (!dir.exists(data_dir)) data_dir <- file.path("dashboard", "data")

esi_file <- file.path(data_dir, "probabilities_esi.csv")
pmi_file <- file.path(data_dir, "probabilities_pmi.csv")

# Default arm: ESI (public data). PMI is shown only if it is the only arm
# available; the backtest (new_code/pseudo_realtime_ESI_vs_PMI.R) decides
# which predictor to feature long-term.
if (file.exists(esi_file)) {
  arm <- "esi"
} else if (file.exists(pmi_file)) {
  arm <- "pmi"
} else {
  arm <- NULL
}

has_data <- !is.null(arm)

if (has_data) {
  probs <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, paste0("probabilities_", arm, ".csv")),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  meta <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, paste0("meta_", arm, ".csv")),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  probs$quarter <- as.yearqtr(probs$quarter, format = "%Y-Q%q")
  probs$geo <- factor(probs$geo, levels = c("EA", "DE", "FR", "IT", "ES"))

  cutoff_quarter <- as.yearqtr(meta$cutoff_quarter, format = "%Y-Q%q")
  max_quarter <- max(probs$quarter)
  window_start <- max_quarter - 10   # last 120 months (40 quarters)

  plot_df <- probs %>%
    filter(quarter >= window_start) %>%
    mutate(
      segment = factor(segment,
                       levels = c("in_sample", "out_of_sample", "nowcast")),
      is_nowcast = segment == "nowcast"
    )

  last_update <- format(as.POSIXct(meta$fitted_at_utc,
                                   tz = "UTC", tryFormats = c("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
                        "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")
}

Dashboard Overview

The chart shows the estimated probability that each economy is in a technical recession (two consecutive quarters of negative quarter-on-quarter GDP growth). The model is trained on data up to the cutoff — five years before the latest available quarter — so the most recent five years are genuinely out-of-sample.

How to Read the Charts

  • Blue line (In-sample): model fit on the training window, shown for the first five years of the 10-year display window.
  • Orange line (Out-of-sample): model probabilities for the held-out last five years, computed with all currently available CISS and sentiment data.
  • Dashed orange line + dot (Nowcast): the extension beyond the last published GDP quarter — quarters whose three months of predictor data are already published but whose GDP outcome is not. This is the model’s current recession-risk reading; it becomes a verified out-of-sample point once GDP is released.
  • Grey shaded bars: quarters actually in a technical recession (ex-post, from published GDP).
  • Red dashed vertical line: the training cutoff (five years before the latest quarter).
Code 
plot_geo <- function(data, region_name, is_main = FALSE) {
  p_data <- data %>% filter(geo == region_name)

  p <- ggplot(p_data, aes(x = zoo::as.Date(quarter))) +
    geom_rect(
      data = p_data %>% filter(recession_actual == 1),
      aes(xmin = zoo::as.Date(quarter) - 45,
          xmax = zoo::as.Date(quarter) + 45,
          ymin = 0, ymax = 1),
      fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.5, inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    geom_ribbon(
      aes(ymin = lower_95, ymax = upper_95, fill = segment),
      alpha = 0.15, linetype = 0
    ) +
    geom_line(aes(y = prob_recession), colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_line(
      data = p_data %>% filter(!is_nowcast),
      aes(y = prob_recession, colour = segment), linewidth = 1
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = p_data %>% filter(is_nowcast),
      aes(y = prob_recession, colour = segment),
      linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed"
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = p_data %>% filter(is_nowcast) %>% slice_tail(n = 1),
      aes(y = prob_recession), colour = "#E37222", size = 2
    ) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = zoo::as.Date(cutoff_quarter),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
    scale_x_date(breaks = pretty_breaks(6)) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c("in_sample" = "#004B87", "out_of_sample" = "#E37222",
                 "nowcast" = "#E37222"),
      labels = c("In-sample (fit)", "Out-of-sample (last 5 yrs)",
                 "Nowcast (no GDP yet)")
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("in_sample" = "#004B87", "out_of_sample" = "#E37222",
                 "nowcast" = "#E37222"),
      labels = c("In-sample (fit)", "Out-of-sample (last 5 yrs)",
                 "Nowcast (no GDP yet)")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = region_name,
      y = "Recession Probability", x = "",
      colour = NULL, fill = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold",
                                size = ifelse(is_main, 16, 12))
    )

  p
}

if (has_data) {
  p_ea <- plot_geo(plot_df, "EA", is_main = TRUE) +
    labs(subtitle = paste0(
      "Grey bars: actual technical recessions. Red dashed line: 5-year training cutoff. ",
      "Predictor: ", toupper(arm), " + CISS."
    ))
  p_de <- plot_geo(plot_df, "DE")
  p_fr <- plot_geo(plot_df, "FR")
  p_it <- plot_geo(plot_df, "IT")
  p_es <- plot_geo(plot_df, "ES")

  country_grid <- (p_de | p_fr) / (p_it | p_es) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")

  final_plot <- p_ea / country_grid + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.5))

  final_plot
} else {
  cat(
    "No dashboard artifacts found (dashboard/data/probabilities_*.csv).\n\n",
    "Generate them on a data host with:\n\n",
    "    DASHBOARD_PREDICTOR=esi Rscript --vanilla new_code/update_dashboard_data.R\n\n",
    "then re-render this site. See new_code/PROD_RUN_ESI_VS_PMI.md and the README.",
    sep = ""
  )
}

  paste0(
    "**Last updated**: ", last_update,
    "  \n**Training cutoff**: ", format(cutoff_quarter, "%Y Q%q"),

Refreshing This Page

The page renders from committed CSV artifacts, so refreshing the forecast is a three-step cycle and never re-runs the model locally:

  1. Update the data + fit (on a host with RJSDMX/brms, e.g. production): DASHBOARD_PREDICTOR=esi Rscript --vanilla new_code/update_dashboard_data.R
  2. Commit the refreshed dashboard/data/probabilities_esi.csv and meta_esi.csv.
  3. Render: make dashboard (or quarto render).

The PMI arm can be produced the same way with DASHBOARD_PREDICTOR=pmi (production only, see new_code/PROD_RUN_ESI_VS_PMI.md); the ESI-vs-PMI backtest decides which specification is featured here.

References

Furno, Francesco, and Domenico Giannone. 2024. “Nowcasting Recession Risk.” Research Methods and Applications on Macroeconomic Forecasting. https://www.amazon.science/publications/nowcasting-recession-risk.
